channel.title: The BlackSheep Journal
channel.description: Notes on real estate, dealership and event media in Ontario from BlackSheep Digital Works.

item.title: Music in listing videos and event reels: the rights behind the soundtrack
item.description: A listing walkthrough or event highlight reel with a popular song on it involves more than one copyright. Here is what Canada's Copyright Act and SOCAN say about songs, recordings and synchronization, and how to choose music you can actually use.

item.title: Do you need a City permit to shoot in Toronto? What the Film Office rules mean for listing and event media
item.description: Toronto's Film Office treats real estate ads, special events and commercial stills differently. Here is when a City permit applies, when it does not, and what to plan for if your shoot spills onto streets, sidewalks or parks.

item.title: Sending event photos and follow-up emails: what Canada's anti-spam law asks of organizers and agents
item.description: A gallery link, a highlight reel or an open-house follow-up can be a commercial electronic message under CASL. Here is what the CRTC's guidance says about consent, identification and unsubscribe, and how to plan event and listing media around it.

item.title: How far can photo editing go? The Competition Act's general impression test for listing and dealership images
item.description: Canada's Competition Act looks at the overall impression an ad creates, not just its literal words, and that includes the pictures. Here is what the Competition Bureau says, and how to edit vehicle and listing photos without crossing the line.

item.title: Canada's October 2026 market in plain numbers: steady prices, more listings, slower sales
item.description: CREA's October 2026 figures show sales edging up from September but well below last year, prices roughly flat and about five months of inventory. Here is what that picture means for sellers deciding how to present a listing this winter.

item.title: Captions and alt text for listing and event media: what Ontario's accessibility rules ask
item.description: If your brokerage, dealership or organization has 50 or more employees in Ontario, the photos and videos on your website fall under AODA web accessibility rules. Here is what that means for alt text, captions and video descriptions.

item.title: Who owns your listing photos? Copyright basics for Ontario agents and sellers
item.description: Paying for listing photos does not automatically make them yours. Here is what Canada's Copyright Act says about who owns commissioned photos, why it changed in 2012, and what to put in writing before the shoot.

item.title: Drones at your event: what organizers need to know about advertised-event rules
item.description: If your festival, market or race is promoted to the public, a drone flying over it needs federal permission first; here is what that involves, how long it takes and how to plan around it.

item.title: The GTA in October 2026 by home type: where buyers had the most choice
item.description: TRREB's October 2026 figures for detached houses, semis, townhouses and condo apartments across the GTA, and what each segment's level of competition means for how a listing should be presented.

item.title: Floor plans and square footage in Ontario listings: where the number comes from matters
item.description: Where Ontario square footage figures come from, why MPAC, builder and floor plan numbers differ, and how a listing floor plan should present size.

item.title: Photographing guests at your event: consent, notice and privacy basics
item.description: What Canada's federal privacy law and the Privacy Commissioner's guidance say about photos and video of guests at corporate events, grand openings and community events, and how organizers can plan for it.

item.title: Listing in winter: how to plan photos around Durham's short days
item.description: In Durham, the sun sets before 4:50 p.m. from mid-November through the solstice. Here is how to schedule a winter listing shoot around the light, and why the quieter December market makes good photos count.

item.title: Inventory photos for Ontario dealerships: what OMVIC's advertising guideline expects from your images
item.description: Vehicle photos and videos are advertising under Ontario's dealer rules. Here is what OMVIC's Advertising Guideline says about stock photos, the actual unit, sold vehicles and social posts, and how to build an inventory shoot around it.

item.title: Durham's October 2026 market, town by town: more choice for buyers, more reason to stand out
item.description: TRREB's October 2026 figures for Durham Region, broken down by municipality, and what a market with roughly three new listings for every sale means for how a home is presented.

item.title: Listing photos and RECO's advertising rules: consent, accuracy and the expiry date
item.description: Listing photos and video are advertising under Ontario's real estate rules. Here is what RECO's bulletins say about consent, accuracy and how long media can stay online.

item.title: Drone shots for your listing: what Canada's rules actually require
item.description: Aerial photos sell the lot, the street and the setting. Here is what Transport Canada requires before a drone goes up over your listing, and the questions to ask whoever flies it.
